data.name: Eternum EX
data.detailed_description:
Eternum Ex is a retro platform video game with the look and feel of the ’80s arcade cabinet games. Titles that have inspired and most influenced its creation are: Bomb Jack (Tehkan, 1984), Ghosts’n Goblins (Capcom, 1985), Baluba-louk no Densetsu (Able, 1986) and Psychic 5 (Jaleco, 1987).

Story


Sir Arthur has gotten old... too old. He has lost everything he had and loved, and with nothing more to lose he leaves for Samarnath, an evil subterranean kingdom (which no knight has ever returned alive) in search of treasures, adventures and the most important: five magical orbs that together provide: the Eternal youth.

Thanks to its progressive difficulty curve, and with a path divided into “worlds” of 5 levels each one, Eternum Ex is challenging, addictive and an ode to the nostalgia of the golden age of arcade games.

Easy to play, hard to master


With a very simple core gameplay mechanics, an increasing difficulty, an exciting and addictive gameplay, and with a very precise control, Eternum Ex is perfect for retro hardcore gamers but also for those who want to start in retro games, and even for those who want to show children how games were when game industry was taking its first steps and gameplay was the most important factor in a video game.

Key Features


• Awesome gameplay (may cause addiction).
• Retro, arcade and platformer 100%
• 16-bit aesthetics
• Memorable soundtrack
• Plenty of different enemies
• 25 Levels
• Special levels with final bosses
• Secrets bonus on each level
• Worldwide “High Score” leaderboard

reviews.review:
If you're a gamer of a certain age, this can be easily summarised: Mario Bros meets Pac-Man meets Ghosts and Goblins.  It has the style of G&G in it's music, looks, and basic attack mechanics for the player, whilst it has the "single screen" platform gameplay of Mario Bros, and the enemy behaviour of Pac-Man (albeit much more defined and "smarter")

For me it's up there with the likes of Bubble Bobble / Pang / Snow Bros / Bombjack / Rainbow Islands etc, as a simple but fun bite-sized experience, that takes a hook and runs with it. 

The aim is straightforward: get all the chests in a level, and then get to a portal. There's a time limit to do so, but it's not super strict, and is only a mild challenge within the game. A more immediate difficulty comes from the enemies who roam around the level, and constantly respawn.

There's ones who run from side to side, but will drop down levels and jump up onto platforms
There's ones that fly and don't follow a set routine
There's invulnerable ones
There's brains that shoot their eyeballs at you
There's eggs that spew out flying maggots

Each type is introduced by themselves to present a different challenge, and then blended later on to mix up the elements you need to be aware of. What starts off as a gentle difficulty level becomes more frantic, as you evade ground enemies, dodge flying ones, and swipe homing eyeballs out of the air, whilst jumping around platforms.

But even the timer, and the enemies, aren't the biggest *fudger*s in this game. No! That would be the traps and collapsing platforms that they introduce. 

You see, I neglected to mention there are chests that require hitting the floor underneath them, by jumping up, to be opened. This process takes 3 three hits to be exact. It doesn't sound a lot does it? As De La Soul told us "Three! It's a magic number!"

But imagine trying to do that whilst avoiding, or battering, zombie hags who amble around like numpties before suddenly lunging screeching at you. So you avoid, or batter, the hag. Some dirty eyeball spitting brain thing has spat it's eyeball at you, but you swipe that mo *fudga* out of the air. You totally rock!

You land on the collapsing platform, and jump up once to strike the breakable chest, before quickly jumping to the next collapsible platform. You repeat the process, and drop to the floor. One more strike to go......

The platforms reappear, and you quickly leap up. 

It's........ 

done! 

Fist pump! 

The moment where, in your triumph, you forget that the platform you just landed on will disappear again, and you fall onto a zombie hag down below, and you die. 

Again.

Just like all those other times where you thought "ah! you piece of pish! I am your master!" and you then died looking like an overconfident fool.

Did Darkest Dungeon not tell us that "overconfidence is a slow and insidious killer", why, yes! It did. And it is so. Except in this game you'll get dead pretty "quick", rather than "slow".

Oh, it will give you lives. It will give you a save, and generous check-pointing. It will give you extra lives, though you have to take risks to get those. A spoonful of sugar helps it's vile, hateful medicine go down, as it kills you in ever different ways. 

And always the fault is only ever your own..... 

Your lives, seemingly so abundant for such an easy proposition, are dropping like flies. Those continues? soon eaten up. And upon losing them all you have to restart the stage. 5 levels per stage, five stages, and five bosses.

Just enough challenge and frustration for you to say "ah! you *fudger*!", but more than enough fun and simplicity in it's challenge to draw you back in for one more quick go. 

The joy of progress, before then getting to a much trickier penultimate boss stage, where it's now a vertically scrolling platformer. That again, starts off easy and becomes quite a tricky *fudger* as it goes on. Once you've done that, you have a boss battle.

And those are tricky *fudgers* too.

Everything. Everything about it. Everything about it means you could easily mistake it for a classic arcade game. The way it plays. The cartoony but detailed sprites. The groovy 8bit style music that has gothic horror if it was filtered through funk sensibilities.   

After a couple of hours spent veering between having a big grin on my face, and wanting to smash my controller against the wall, I had reached stage 3, and got stuck.

That's about halfway through the content, and for what it's given me in terms of satisfaction, even at this stage I'd say it's totally worth it.

There's leaderboards if you want to pursue getting high scores, and for the achievement hunters it's easy to get loads, as one is handed out for completing levels / stages etc. They're not difficult to get generally, other than obviously having to finish the game.

And you will be likely to want to finish it, as whilst the challenge is tough, it's not unfairly so. The game will entice you one more time, and you'll do better. At least up until the point where you die again, and you tell yourself "Right! That's it. I'm not playing it anymore"

But that's a big fat lie.....you know you're going to play it again. The triumph, the glory...it's so close. Just one more go, and you will overcome this oh so simple thing that has vexed you....

Probably.....

<forgets that collapsible platforms can be jumped up through, and gets killed by something that looks like a cross between a piranha and an aubergine>

"oh you *fudger*!"

<Rage quits thinking about Eternum Ex anymore. Review ends>
